cross_functional.what: Leading a team you don't manage: engineering, design, data, marketing, sales, legal, all pulling toward one outcome.

subskills.name: Working the product triad
subskills.example: Plan, decide, and review as a trio of PM, EM, and design lead.

subskills.name: Driving alignment
subskills.example: Write down who decides what before the first disagreement.

subskills.name: Rituals & cadence
subskills.example: One weekly sync with a written agenda and decisions log.

subskills.name: Partnering beyond product
subskills.example: Loop legal in at the spec stage, not the week before launch.

ladder.associate: Works well within a squad; keeps partners informed.
ladder.mid: Leads a squad's cross-functional work; resolves routine conflicts.
ladder.senior: Leads across several teams and functions on big initiatives.
ladder.lead: Builds the operating model for how functions work together.

build: Any team project where you coordinate people you don't control (student orgs, hackathons, volunteer work) counts; write up how you ran it.
Read: 'Team Topologies' on how teams interact; 'The Making of a Manager' on leading without authority.
At work: run the weekly sync for a cross-functional project and keep the decision log.
signals: Led a 25-person cross-functional launch across 4 teams and 3 time zones.
Introduced a decision log and DACI model that halved re-litigated decisions.

stakeholder_mgmt.what: Keeping the people who can block or accelerate your work informed, heard, and on side: executives, partner teams, customers.

subskills.name: Stakeholder mapping
subskills.example: List who cares, who decides, and who can block, before kickoff.

subskills.name: Managing up
subskills.example: Leadership hears bad news from you first, with a plan attached.

subskills.name: Expectation setting
subskills.example: Commit to dates with ranges and say what would move them.

subskills.name: Conflict & difficult conversations
subskills.example: Address the disagreement directly in a 1:1, not in the group thread.

ladder.associate: Keeps their stakeholders updated; escalates early.
ladder.mid: Manages a defined set of stakeholders; handles pushback on scope.
ladder.senior: Manages senior stakeholders with conflicting agendas.
ladder.lead: Manages executives and the board; brokers org-level trade-offs.

build: Read: 'Crucial Conversations'; 'Getting to Yes' for negotiation.
Practice: before any proposal, write each stakeholder's likely objection and your answer.
At work: own the status update to leadership for a project for a quarter.
signals: Managed 8 stakeholders across sales, legal, and finance through a contentious pricing change.
Ran the monthly exec update for the platform program with no surprises for a year.

influence.what: Getting people to change course without being able to tell them to: evidence, framing, relationships, and timing.

subskills.name: Persuasive writing & framing
subskills.example: Lead with the customer problem and the cost of inaction.

subskills.name: Evidence-based arguments
subskills.example: Bring three customer recordings and one chart, not opinions.

subskills.name: Building coalitions
subskills.example: Pre-wire the decision 1:1 so the meeting is a confirmation.

subskills.name: Negotiation
subskills.example: Trade a scope cut for a firm engineering commitment.

ladder.associate: Makes clear, evidence-backed cases for small decisions.
ladder.mid: Wins support for team priorities across peer teams.
ladder.senior: Changes direction at the org level through persuasion, not authority.
ladder.lead: Shapes company direction; influences executives and the board.

build: Read: 'Influence' (Cialdini), 'Never Split the Difference'.
Practice: write a one-page memo arguing for a change and get feedback from someone who disagrees.
At work: pick one decision you want reversed and run a deliberate influence campaign.
signals: Persuaded engineering leadership to fund the platform rebuild through a customer-evidence memo.
Built the coalition that moved the company to usage-based pricing.

communication.what: Writing and speaking so that busy people understand, remember, and act: clear, short, structured, and matched to the audience.

subskills.name: Writing clear documents
subskills.example: One page, conclusion first, every paragraph earns its place.

subskills.name: Presenting
subskills.example: A 10-slide deck where the title of each slide is the point.

subskills.name: Tailoring to the audience
subskills.example: Same decision, three versions: engineers, executives, customers.

subskills.name: Async & written updates
subskills.example: A Friday update in five bullets: done, next, blocked, decisions, asks.

subskills.name: Listening & facilitation
subskills.example: Run the meeting so the quiet expert talks and the decision gets made.

ladder.associate: Writes clear tickets and updates; presents to the team.
ladder.mid: Writes PRDs and memos that need little clarification; presents to leadership.
ladder.senior: Known for writing that changes decisions; presents to executives and customers.
ladder.lead: Sets communication norms for the org; speaks for the product externally.

build: Course: Google's technical writing courses (free); a presentation skills class or Toastmasters.
Practice: rewrite a long email to half its length; write a weekly update for a side project.
At work: volunteer to write the launch memo or present the quarterly review.
signals: Wrote the 6-pager that secured funding for the new product line.
Presented the roadmap to 300 customers at the user conference.

exec_communication.what: Communicating with executives and boards: the brief, the business review, and the ask, in the little time they have.

subskills.name: Executive briefs
subskills.example: Decision needed, recommendation, three reasons, risks, ask. Half a page.

subskills.name: Business reviews
subskills.example: Metrics vs. plan, why, what we're doing, what we need.

subskills.name: Board & investor communication
subskills.example: Board slides: the trend, the risk, the ask, nothing else.

subskills.name: Executive presence
subskills.example: Answer the question asked, then stop.

ladder.associate: Contributes slides to reviews; presents a section with support.
ladder.mid: Presents their area in leadership reviews.
ladder.senior: Runs business reviews; briefs executives regularly.
ladder.lead: Presents to the board; is the executive audience for others.

build: Read: 'The Pyramid Principle' (Minto) for structure; study Amazon-style narrative memos.
Practice: turn any analysis into a half-page exec brief with a decision at the top.
At work: ask to present your area's section of the next leadership review.
signals: Presented the product section of the quarterly board deck for two years.
Ran the monthly business review for a $40M product line.

people_management.what: Hiring, developing, and leading product managers: building the team, setting the bar, and growing people.

subskills.name: Hiring & interviewing
subskills.example: A structured loop with a product-sense case and a written exercise.

subskills.name: Coaching & feedback
subskills.example: Weekly 1:1s focused on their growth, not status.

subskills.name: Performance management
subskills.example: Clear written expectations per level and honest calibration.

subskills.name: Building & structuring teams
subskills.example: Design team boundaries around products, not technologies.

subskills.name: Leading managers
subskills.example: Run skip-levels and hold managers to how they grow their people.

ladder.associate: Mentors interns or new hires informally.
ladder.mid: Mentors junior PMs; participates in hiring loops.
ladder.senior: Leads a small team of PMs or formally mentors several; owns part of the hiring bar.
ladder.lead: Manages PMs and managers; owns hiring, leveling, and org design.

build: Read: 'The Making of a Manager' (Zhuo), 'High Output Management' (Grove).
Practice: mentor someone (ADPList, a university program) and ask for feedback on your coaching.
At work: become an interviewer, then a hiring manager for an intern or APM.
signals: Hired and managed a team of 6 PMs; promoted 2 to senior in 18 months.
Designed the PM leveling framework adopted across the org.

ownership.what: Treating outcomes as yours: driving work to done, taking responsibility when it goes wrong, and not waiting to be told.

subskills.name: Owning outcomes, not tasks
subskills.example: Own the activation rate, not the ticket about the onboarding screen.

subskills.name: Taking initiative
subskills.example: Notice the gap, propose the fix, start before you're asked.

subskills.name: Follow-through
subskills.example: Every open thread has an owner and a date, and you check.

subskills.name: Scrappiness & resourcefulness
subskills.example: Write the support macro yourself if that's what ships it.

ladder.associate: Owns their tickets and features to done; flags risks early.
ladder.mid: Owns a product area's outcomes; is the person people ask.
ladder.senior: Owns results across teams; takes accountability publicly.
ladder.lead: Owns business outcomes; sets the ownership culture.

build: Ship a side project end to end, including the boring parts (support, docs, fixes).
At work: pick a problem nobody owns, write the plan, and run it.
Keep a 'things I drove to done' log; that becomes your resume.
signals: Took over the stalled migration project and delivered it in one quarter.
Owned day-30 retention; ran 11 experiments and moved it from 28% to 36%.

adaptability.what: Working well when the plan changes: ambiguity, pace, pivots, and growth that outruns process.

subskills.name: Comfort with ambiguity
subskills.example: Start from a one-paragraph brief and have a plan by Friday.

subskills.name: Pace & iteration speed
subskills.example: Ship the 80% version this week instead of the 100% version next month.

subskills.name: Pivoting & learning
subskills.example: Drop the plan when the data says so, and say why.

subskills.name: Wearing many hats
subskills.example: PM, support, QA, and analyst in the same week at an early startup.

ladder.associate: Handles changing priorities without losing track.
ladder.mid: Thrives on under-specified problems; keeps the team steady through change.
ladder.senior: Leads through pivots; builds just enough process for the stage.
ladder.lead: Steers the org through strategy changes and scaling pains.

build: Join or build something early-stage: a startup, a hackathon team, a student venture.
Keep a log of times the plan changed and what you did next.
At work: volunteer for the undefined project or the new team.
signals: Joined as employee #12; built the product function from zero through Series B.
Led the pivot from consumer to B2B; shipped the new product in 4 months.

collaboration.what: Being good to work with: generous with credit, open to being wrong, and reliable to the people around you.

subskills.name: Building relationships
subskills.example: Know what each partner is measured on and help them hit it.

subskills.name: Giving & receiving feedback
subskills.example: Ask 'what would make this better' and mean it.

subskills.name: Low ego & humility
subskills.example: Change your mind in the meeting when the engineer is right.

subskills.name: Inclusive teamwork
subskills.example: Make room for the person who hasn't spoken.

ladder.mid: Builds strong partnerships with their triad and adjacent teams.
ladder.senior: Sought out as a partner; raises the team's collaboration norms.
ladder.lead: Sets the culture for how teams treat each other.

build: Any sustained team experience counts: sports, bands, open-source, student orgs.
Read: 'Radical Candor' for feedback; 'The Five Dysfunctions of a Team'.
At work: ask three partners for honest feedback and act on one thing.
signals: Named 'most collaborative partner' by engineering in two consecutive surveys.
Built the product/sales feedback loop that both teams credit for the SMB turnaround.

customer_facing_exec.what: Representing the product to the outside world: customer executives, advisory boards, conferences, analysts, and press.

subskills.name: Customer executive engagement
subskills.example: Run an executive briefing that's about their roadmap, not yours.

subskills.name: Advisory boards & councils
subskills.example: Quarterly CAB with real decisions on the table.

subskills.name: Public speaking & events
subskills.example: A 20-minute talk with one idea the audience repeats afterwards.

subskills.name: Analysts, press & thought leadership
subskills.example: Brief analysts twice a year with a clear differentiation story.

ladder.associate: Joins customer calls; writes blog posts.
ladder.mid: Presents to customers; runs feature-level briefings.
ladder.senior: Runs advisory boards; speaks at conferences; briefs analysts.
ladder.lead: Is the public face of the product; handles press and key executives.

build: Speak: local meetups, internal brown-bags, Toastmasters.
Write: a blog or newsletter on your product area; that's thought leadership in miniature.
At work: ask to present at the next customer event or run a customer council.
signals: Ran the 20-member customer advisory board for three years.
Spoke at four industry conferences; briefed Gartner for the Magic Quadrant.

agile_scrum.what: Running delivery in short iterations: backlog, sprints, ceremonies, and the discipline that keeps them useful.

subskills.name: Sprint planning & backlog
subskills.example: A sprint goal in one sentence and a backlog ready two sprints ahead.

subskills.name: Ceremonies
subskills.example: Retros that produce one change each, and you check it stuck.

subskills.name: Scaled frameworks
subskills.example: Know PI planning if you're in a large enterprise; know its costs.

subskills.name: Kanban & flow
subskills.example: Limit WIP and watch cycle time instead of velocity.

ladder.associate: Writes stories, keeps the board current, runs standup.
ladder.mid: Owns the backlog and sprint goals for a squad.
ladder.senior: Tailors process to the team; fixes delivery problems at the root.
ladder.lead: Sets delivery practices across teams; avoids process for its own sake.

build: Course: a Scrum or Product Owner certification (CSPO/PSPO) is cheap and often asked for in enterprises.
Project: run a side project in two-week sprints with a board and retros.
At work: run backlog refinement and the retro for a quarter.
signals: Certified Scrum Product Owner; ran delivery for two squads.
Moved the team from scrum to kanban; cycle time fell from 12 days to 5.

program_mgmt.what: Coordinating large, multi-team efforts: plans, milestones, dependencies, status, and getting the whole thing to land.

subskills.name: Planning & milestones
subskills.example: A milestone plan with the critical path marked and owners per stream.

subskills.name: Dependency management
subskills.example: A dependency list reviewed weekly with the teams you depend on.

subskills.name: Status & reporting
subskills.example: A weekly one-pager: green/amber/red, why, what's needed.

subskills.name: Governance & operating rhythm
subskills.example: A monthly steering meeting with decisions, not status.

subskills.name: Large launch coordination
subskills.example: A cut-over plan with go/no-go criteria and a rollback owner.

ladder.associate: Tracks tasks and status for a project; keeps the plan current.
ladder.mid: Runs a multi-team program: plan, dependencies, status, risks.
ladder.senior: Runs org-wide programs with executive sponsors; fixes structural delivery problems.
ladder.lead: Builds the program function; owns the company's biggest initiatives.

build: Course: PMP or Google's Project Management certificate for vocabulary and tools.
Project: plan and run a multi-person event or build with a real plan, risks, and status updates.
At work: offer to run the program for the next cross-team initiative.
signals: Ran the 9-month data-center migration across 12 teams; delivered on date.
Introduced weekly RAG reporting and a steering committee for the platform program.

risk_mgmt.what: Seeing what could go wrong early, deciding what to do about it, and escalating before it becomes a crisis.

subskills.name: Identifying risks
subskills.example: A pre-mortem before kickoff: 'it's six months later and it failed; why?'

subskills.name: Mitigation & contingency
subskills.example: Each top risk has an owner, a trigger, and a plan B.

subskills.name: Escalation
subskills.example: Escalate with options, not just the problem, and early.

subskills.name: Unblocking
subskills.example: Spend your week removing the one thing the team is stuck on.

ladder.associate: Flags risks in their area and keeps a simple risk list.
ladder.mid: Owns the risk register for a program; mitigates and escalates.
ladder.senior: Anticipates cross-team and business risks; shapes contingency plans.
ladder.lead: Sets risk tolerance and escalation norms for the org.

build: Practice: run a pre-mortem on any plan you make.
Course: risk management is a module in most PM certifications.
At work: keep the risk register for your project and review it in the weekly sync.
signals: Identified the vendor dependency risk three months early; secured a second supplier.
Ran pre-mortems on all tier-1 launches; zero launch-day rollbacks in 2024.

execution.what: Getting things done reliably and well: driving to outcomes, holding quality, and keeping the details from slipping.

subskills.name: Driving to done
subskills.example: Every project has a date, an owner, and a weekly check.

subskills.name: Attention to detail
subskills.example: Check the empty state, the error copy, and the email template yourself.

subskills.name: Operational excellence
subskills.example: Launch checklists, dashboards, and a post-launch review, every time.

subskills.name: Results orientation
subskills.example: Report what changed for customers and the business, not what shipped.

ladder.associate: Delivers features on time with few surprises.
ladder.mid: Reliably lands quarter-sized initiatives with quality.
ladder.senior: Lands big, multi-team bets; known as someone who ships.
ladder.lead: Builds an org that executes; sets the quality bar.

build: Ship things: side projects, open-source contributions, anything with a 'done' state.
Keep a results log: what you delivered, when, and what it changed.
At work: take a slipping project and get it back on track.
signals: Shipped 9 of 9 committed H1 initiatives; two ahead of schedule.
Known for launch quality: zero rollbacks across 20 releases.

process_improvement.what: Designing how work gets done so it scales: operating cadence, mechanisms, playbooks, and removing waste.

subskills.name: Operating cadence & mechanisms
subskills.example: Quarterly planning, monthly reviews, weekly syncs, each with a doc.

subskills.name: Playbooks & templates
subskills.example: A launch playbook anyone can run without you.

subskills.name: Lean & waste removal
subskills.example: Map the process, find the bottleneck, fix that first.

subskills.name: Scaling process with the org
subskills.example: Add process only when its absence is costing more than it would.

ladder.associate: Follows and improves the team's templates.
ladder.mid: Designs the operating cadence for their team.
ladder.senior: Builds mechanisms used across teams; removes systemic waste.

build: Course: a lean or operations management intro (many MBA cores are online).
Project: document and improve any recurring process you're part of; measure the time saved.
At work: write the playbook for something your team does repeatedly.
signals: Built the product operating cadence (planning, reviews, launches) for a 40-person org.
Cut launch prep time 50% with a standardized playbook and checklist.

quality_testing.what: Making sure what ships works: test plans, acceptance, beta programs, and the quality bar before and after launch.

subskills.name: Test plans & acceptance
subskills.example: Write the acceptance tests with the spec; run UAT yourself.

subskills.name: Bug triage & prioritization
subskills.example: Weekly triage with clear severity rules; P1s block release.

subskills.name: Beta & dogfooding
subskills.example: Dogfood for two weeks before any customer sees it.

subskills.name: Quality metrics
subskills.example: Track escaped bugs per release and the top causes.

ladder.associate: Writes acceptance criteria and tests features before release.
ladder.mid: Owns the quality bar for their features; runs bug triage.
ladder.senior: Sets quality standards for a product; owns beta and dogfood programs.
ladder.lead: Sets the org's quality bar and release criteria.

build: Course: an intro to software testing (ISTQB foundation material is free).
Project: write a test plan for a feature you use and find three bugs.
At work: run the bug bash for the next release.
signals: Instituted release criteria and bug bashes; escaped P1s fell 70%.
Ran a 200-customer beta program for the redesign.

vendor_mgmt.what: Buying and managing what you don't build: vendor selection, contracts, SLAs, and budgets.

subskills.name: Vendor evaluation & selection
subskills.example: A scored RFP with a hands-on proof of concept for the finalists.

subskills.name: Contracts & SLAs
subskills.example: Negotiate SLAs with teeth and an exit clause.

subskills.name: Budget management
subskills.example: Own the budget line and forecast it quarterly.

subskills.name: Ongoing vendor management
subskills.example: Quarterly reviews against the SLA with escalation paths.

ladder.mid: Runs a vendor evaluation; manages one or two vendor relationships.
ladder.senior: Owns build-vs-buy decisions and major contracts for a product.
ladder.lead: Owns vendor strategy and budget across products.

build: Course: procurement or negotiation basics.
Project: write an RFP for a tool category you know and score three vendors.
At work: run the next tool evaluation for your team end to end.
signals: Ran the RFP and negotiation for the analytics vendor; saved 30% vs. list.
Managed $2M in vendor contracts with quarterly SLA reviews.

jira.what: The work-tracking and documentation tools product teams run on.

subskills.name: Jira / Linear / Asana workflows
subskills.example: Set up the board, workflows, and automation your team actually uses.

subskills.name: Confluence / Notion documentation
subskills.example: A single, findable home for specs, decisions, and runbooks.

subskills.name: Roadmapping tools
subskills.example: Connect feedback to roadmap items so prioritization has a trail.

build: Set up a free Jira or Linear workspace for a side project and run it properly.
At work: become the person who maintains the team's board and templates.
signals: Administered Jira for a 60-person org; built the intake and triage workflows.
Set up Productboard to link 2,000 feedback items to roadmap themes.

figma.what: Design and whiteboarding tools well enough to sketch, prototype, and collaborate with designers.

subskills.name: Figma for wireframes & prototypes
subskills.example: Build a clickable prototype from the design system components.

subskills.name: Whiteboarding (Miro, FigJam)
subskills.example: Run a remote mapping workshop in FigJam.

build: Figma's own tutorials; recreate three screens of an app you like.
At work: wireframe your next feature before briefing design.
signals: Prototyped the onboarding redesign in Figma; validated with 8 users before build.
Facilitated journey-mapping workshops in Miro with 20 stakeholders.

analytics_tools.what: Product analytics and BI tools: setting up tracking, building dashboards, running analyses.

subskills.name: Product analytics (Amplitude, Mixpanel, Pendo)
subskills.example: Build the funnel and retention charts yourself; set up the events.

subskills.name: BI tools (Looker, Tableau, Power BI)
subskills.example: Own the team dashboard in Looker and the model behind it.

subskills.name: Web analytics (GA4)
subskills.example: Attribute signups to channels with UTM discipline.

build: Amplitude and Mixpanel both have free tiers and free certification courses.
Project: instrument a side project and build a funnel, retention, and feature-usage dashboard.
At work: build your own dashboards instead of requesting them.
signals: Amplitude-certified; built the activation funnel and retention dashboards used by 5 teams.
Built the Looker explore for product usage; analyst requests dropped 60%.

experimentation_tools.what: Platforms for running experiments and controlling rollouts.

subskills.name: Experimentation platforms
subskills.example: Configure the test, metrics, and exposure yourself.

subskills.name: Feature flags & rollouts
subskills.example: Use flags for staged rollouts and kill switches, not just tests.

build: Set up GrowthBook or Statsig's free tier on a side project and run one test.
At work: own the experiment configuration for your team's tests.
signals: Ran 30+ tests in Statsig; built the team's experiment review template.
Introduced LaunchDarkly for staged rollouts across the mobile app.

office_tools.what: Spreadsheets and slides at a level that supports real analysis and persuasion.

subskills.name: Advanced spreadsheets
subskills.example: Build a model with scenarios, pivots, and a clean summary tab.

subskills.name: Slides & decks
subskills.example: A deck where every slide title is the takeaway.

build: Any spreadsheet modelling course; practice by rebuilding a public company's unit economics.
At work: own the planning model and the quarterly review deck.
signals: Built the capacity-planning model in Sheets used across 8 teams.
Produced the board-level product deck each quarter.

crm_tools.what: Sales and customer tools: reading pipeline, pulling customer data, and understanding how the field works.

subskills.name: CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot)
subskills.example: Pull win/loss and pipeline by segment from the CRM yourself.

subskills.name: Call intelligence & support tools
subskills.example: Search Gong for every call that mentions your feature.

build: Trailhead (Salesforce's free training) for CRM basics.
At work: get read access to the CRM and support tool and use them weekly.
signals: Built the Salesforce report that tracks feature-request mentions by deal size.
Reviewed 50 Gong calls per quarter to feed roadmap planning.

ai_tools.what: Using AI tools in daily product work: prototyping, analysis, writing, and research, faster than before.

subskills.name: AI-assisted prototyping
subskills.example: Build a working prototype of the feature in an afternoon to test with users.

subskills.name: AI for analysis & synthesis
subskills.example: Synthesize 40 interview transcripts with an LLM, then verify by hand.

subskills.name: AI-native workflows
subskills.example: Automate the weekly update draft from the ticket tracker.

build: Build something with Cursor, Claude Code, or Replit this week; the only way to learn is to use them.
Project: prototype a feature idea with AI tools and test it with 5 users.
At work: pick one recurring task and automate it with an LLM.
signals: Prototyped 6 feature concepts with AI tools in Q1; 2 shipped after user tests.
Built an LLM pipeline that tags and summarizes support tickets daily.
